name: TDC ADMET hERG
description: Predict whether a compound blocks the hERG potassium channel of the heart (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint hERG of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the ROC curve on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.

sources.locator: ADMET Evaluation in Drug Discovery. 16. Predicting hERG Blockers by Combining Multiple Pharmacophores and Machine Learning Approaches
hERG blockers: binary classification, 648 drugs, reference Wang et al. 2016 Mol Pharm.

Huang et al. (2022), Artificial intelligence foundation for therapeutic science (Nat Chem Biol): the Therapeutics Data Commons paper linked from the TDC site, benchmark paper only; also arXiv 2102.09548, Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development.

requirements.datasets: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: a score that is larger for class 1 (for example its probability). train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the area under the ROC curve on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

limitations: Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

checks: leaderboard rank 1 (AUROC): MapLight + GNN Jim Notwell 0.88

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: The cited paper(s) have the prediction or measurement of this property as their main objective; the task scores a structure-based predictor of the same property.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify molecules as blockers or non-blockers of the hERG potassium channel from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Blocking the hERG channel prolongs the cardiac QT interval and can cause fatal arrhythmia, and it is a common reason for drug attrition and withdrawal, so it is screened for early.

papers.title: ADMET Evaluation in Drug Discovery. 16. Predicting hERG Blockers by Combining Multiple Pharmacophores and Machine Learning Approaches
papers.task_relation: The task asks for the blocker/non-blocker label on the 648-compound set of this paper; local split and metric differ.
papers.primary_goal: Predict hERG channel blockers from molecular structure by combining multiple pharmacophore models with machine learning.
